$comment: Every dataset a query can read, declared once and loaded by every query engine (AW-3): Flow through services/query/flow/src/Dataset/CatalogFile.php, DataFusion and DuckDB through aiwatcher_query. The columns are the contract, not documentation — each engine projects exactly these and refuses a reference to anything else. A key a loader does not know is refused rather than defaulted; "$comment" is the one key every level skips.

datasets.name: runs
datasets.description: Runs the projector still retains, newest first. The default: it is the grain the explorer tree shows, and the fast one.

hints.$comment: The single most likely first query, and the one place this dataset's shape surprises people.
hints.agent: A run can involve several agents, so the column is "agents", a list. For one row per run and agent, add ->withEntry('agent', array_expand(ref('agents'))) before the groupBy. For one row per span with a single agent, read the "spans" dataset instead.
hints.runtime: A run can be produced by several services, so the column is "runtimes", a list. Add ->withEntry('runtime', array_expand(ref('runtimes'))) before the groupBy.
hints.model: A run does not carry the models it used; its spans do. Read the "spans" dataset.
hints.tool: A run does not carry the tools it called; its spans do. Read the "spans" dataset.

datasets.name: spans
datasets.description: Every retained span, flat. Each row has exactly one agent, model and tool, so this is the dataset to group by any of them.

datasets.name: events
datasets.description: The raw log for one run, from the durable log rather than the read model. Needs a run: read(events, run: 'run-1').

datasets.$comment: The hub search is capped rather than paged — the answer to four hundred matches is a narrower query, not a cursor — so there is no next_cursor in the body and cursor_param is never replayed. claimed_license is named for what it is: a mirror's licence field is what somebody typed when uploading a copy.
datasets.name: hub_datasets
datasets.grain: one row per dataset a hub says it has
datasets.description: Kaggle and Hugging Face, searched live. A discovery surface, never a licence: every row is usage "unclear" unless it matches a corpus whose licence a human read at the original.

hints.license: The column is "claimed_license", and the name is the point: it is the mirror's word, not a licence. "usage" is aiwatcher's verdict and is "unclear" unless "curated_source" names a corpus somebody read at the original.
hints.name: The columns are "id" (owner/name, how the hub addresses it) and "title".
hints.files: The search does not list files. Open the dataset at its "url".

parameters.$comment: q, not search: a parameter's name is what goes on the wire, and this route spells it q where the annotation routes spell theirs search. Declared wrongly it is a 400 from aiwatcher rather than a refusal while the query is read.
parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text. Omitted asks each hub what it considers popular, which is a worse question than any real one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per hub, capped at 50 by the API.

datasets.$comment: This route has offsets rather than next_cursor, and a read pages a bounded sample: read(limit: 891) must not silently return 100. row_index is where the row sat in the split — the only name it has that the corpus did not choose, and usually what a per-picture family key is built from. row is every column of the corpus under its own name. omitted names the columns the API left out: one the hub itself shortened, or one too large to carry.
datasets.name: hub_rows
datasets.grain: one row of one hub dataset, as the hub sent it
datasets.description: The contents of one Hugging Face dataset. The search says which corpora exist; this says what is in one — with the corpus's own columns under the corpus's own names. Which column is the picture, what the caption is called and what a family key is built from are decided here, in the query, because they are questions about that corpus.

hints.columns: The corpus's own columns are inside "row", under its own names, and are not listed here because they belong to the dataset being read rather than to this catalog. Reach one with array_get(ref('row'), '<name>'), which takes a dot path into a structure. A column holding bytes is named in address: on the read() and comes back as an address this API resolves.
hints.uri: Whatever you name it. The import reads "uri", "width", "height" and "group_id" from the columns this query produces.
hints.license: Not here. A licence is a property of the corpus, which is the hub_datasets row.

parameters.name: dataset
parameters.description: owner/name, exactly as a hub_datasets row addresses it.

parameters.name: hub
parameters.description: Only Hugging Face serves rows; Kaggle publishes archives and is refused.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The dataset configuration. Discovered when absent.

parameters.name: split
parameters.description: The split to read. Discovered when absent.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Where in the split to start.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Total rows to read (1–1000, default 100), fetched in pages of at most 100.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Columns to receive as an address instead of a value, comma-separated. This is where "which column holds bytes" is decided, and it is decided here: a hub calling a column binary says it is a byte string, not that it is a picture. Without it every column comes as it came — and a column of base64 pictures is then dropped for its size and named in "omitted".

datasets.$comment: The same route as hub_rows, read for its envelope instead of its rows: what the corpus declares it holds, which is what a hub_rows query has to be written against. kind is the hub's own type tag, verbatim — empty where the hub describes a column with a nested structure instead of a tag.
datasets.name: hub_columns
datasets.grain: one row per column a hub dataset declares
datasets.description: What a Hugging Face dataset says its columns are, in its own words. Read this first when writing a hub_rows query: it is where the column names come from, and it is the hub's answer rather than aiwatcher's.

hints.image: There is no such column here either. "kind" and "dtype" are the hub's words — Image, Value, binary, string — and which of them holds a picture is a judgement about the corpus.
hints.type: The columns are "kind" (the hub's type tag) and "dtype" (what a Value carries).

parameters.name: dataset
parameters.description: owner/name, exactly as a hub_datasets row addresses it.

parameters.name: config
parameters.description: The dataset configuration. Discovered when absent.

parameters.name: split
parameters.description: The split to read. Discovered when absent.

datasets.$comment: group_id is the subject, not the picture: a mirrored or re-shot copy shares it with its original, which is what keeps them on one side of the split.
datasets.name: annotation_images
datasets.description: What an annotation project already holds. The dataset an import pipeline joins against so a second run of it does not re-register what the first one did.

hints.project: The project is a read() argument, not a column: read(annotation_images, project: 'corpora/first').
hints.rights: Not projected here; rights is a tagged object rather than a column. Read one image for it.
hints.family: The column is "group_id" — the subject, however many pictures of it there are.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Which annotation project to read. There is no route without one.

parameters.name: review
parameters.description: Only images in this review state.

parameters.name: split
parameters.description: Only one side of the family split.

datasets.name: corpus_spans
datasets.grain: one row per span, from part files on disk
datasets.description: The benchmark corpus under AIWATCHER_CORPUS_DIR: synthetic spans as CSV or Parquet parts, read by Flow directly rather than through the API. Gigabytes, so a query over all of it takes minutes: run it on the server rather than as a preview.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Which copy to read: the CSV the size is quoted in (the default), or the same rows as Parquet.
